title: Mini integrator heuristic notebook
body:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact, pragmatic notebook for field engineers and integrators who need a light-weight, telemetry-first onramp to Redwood SDKs. The intent is not to be a canonical guide (that lives in docs/) but a short, opinionated playbook we can hand to an engineer pairing with a customer or running a 60–90 minute integration lab.

Scope and constraints (quick):
- Focus: first integration, telemetry + failure-observability, and three micro-labs (hello-gen, streaming, embed-and-cache).
- Constraints: 30–90 minute hands-on window; minimal infra/setup; no production secrets.
- Outcome targets: working hello-gen demo, basic telemetry events emitted, and a reproducible checklist for follow-up.

High-level flows (1-liners):
1) Local smoke: set API key env var -> call /responses/generate -> confirm 200 and token_count metric.
2) Telemetry probe: enable SDK debug flag -> emit trace id -> surface in console + CloudWatch/local collector.
3) Failure-handling lab: simulate rate-limit -> validate retry/backoff policy logs and fallback to cached response.

Preflight checklist (prep before running with customer):
- [ ] Install latest stable SDK (recommended tag: v0.8.3).
- [ ] Have temp API key with read-only quota and basic telemetry enabled.
- [ ] Sample app repo cloned and test credentials ready.
- [ ] Local collector: run a simple OTLP collector or point to our sandbox logging endpoint.
- [ ] Confirm port 4317 outbound allowed (OTLP) or plan console-only telemetry.

Micro-lab 1: Hello-gen (10–15 min)
Goal: 1 request -> 1 streaming or chunked response showing timings.
Steps (commands/snippets):
- Set env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
- Minimal Node example (pseudo):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const c = new Redwood.Client({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, debug: true});
  const r = await c.generate({model: 'redwood-alpha-7b', prompt: 'Write a haiku about coffee.'});
  console.log(r.text, r.metrics.token_count);
Observability checks:
- confirm debug logs show request_id and model_latency_ms
- check telemetry collector for metric: redwood.requests.count (labels: model, status)
- verify token_count > 0
Pitfalls seen in the wild:
- Missing environment variables -> opaque auth error. Remedy: quick env-vars diagnostic snippet (print out REDWOOD_API_KEY masked).
- Local dev proxies blocking streaming responses -> test with curl first.

Micro-lab 2: Streaming + cancel (15–20 min)
Goal: Stream response and exercise client-side cancellation and graceful fallback.
Pattern:
- Start streaming with SDK stream API. After 400ms cancel the stream and capture partial tokens.
- On cancellation, emit telemetry event: redwood.stream.cancel with reason and time_ms.
Example heuristics:
- If >60% of requests are cancelled within 200ms, assume mismatch: sample heavy prompt or reduce gen_max_tokens.

Micro-lab 3: Embedding + prefix cache probe (20–25 min)
Goal: Show how embedding calls can be cached and how to detect cache hits via telemetry.
Steps:
- Compute embedding for sample doc set (<=10 docs).
- Use local LRU cache wrapper with key = model + sha256(text).
- Emit telemetry tag on each embedding request: embedding.cache_status = hit|miss
Observation to capture:
- hit_ratio should rise after repeated queries; if not, check key normalization (trimming, unicode normalization).

Telemetry events and minimal schema (recommended for quick labs):
- redwood.request.start {request_id, model, route}
- redwood.request.end {request_id, model, status, token_count, latency_ms}
- redwood.stream.chunk {request_id, seq, bytes}
- redwood.stream.cancel {request_id, reason, time_ms}
- redwood.embedding.cache_status {key, hit_or_miss}
Keep events lightweight (string labels + numeric metrics).

Failure injection scenarios (quick cleans):
- 429 (rate limit): verify client retries with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts and emits redwood.retry.event (attempts).
- Network jitter: add 150–500ms latency to SDK calls; observe how batching/latency SLOs change.
- Model fallback: configure fallback to a smaller quantized model; validate that telemetry shows fallback=true and request latency increases/decreases appropriately.

Short checklist to hand the customer after session:
- [ ] Confirm sample repo forked and token rotated (if shared).
- [ ] Telemetry events flowing to customer/Redwood sandbox endpoint.
- [ ] Create follow-up ticket with sample logs + request_ids for 2 failing cases.
- [ ] Schedule 1-hour architecture sync to discuss productionizing caching and rollout policy.

Open questions / hypotheses to test later:
- Can we add a one-click telemetry toggle in the SDK that auto-configures an OTLP exporter pointed to our sandbox? (reduces prep time)
- Should our quickstart default to a lower-cost quantized model to prevent early quota blowouts?
- What are the minimum telemetry labels customers need to correlate logs to traces across our console?

To-dos (short-term):
- [ ] Convert example snippets into runnable gist and link in customer-facing quickstart. (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Add a tiny OTLP collector Docker compose file to sample repo (owner: Leah).
- [ ] Draft a short SLO checklist for 1st-month production (owner: Aisha).

Slack/links for follow-ups: #eng-devexp-onramp, #customers-pilot, linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412

Notes to self (raw/fragmented):
- Keep labs <90m.
- Prefer streaming demo first (more 'wow').
- Telemetry is the defender: if operator can't see request_id -> no trust.

End of notebook.
